input.reason: Audited slugify/slugify.js against slugify/SPEC.md by code reading plus runtime checks. Two spec rules are violated with reproducible inputs; module.exports.slugify is otherwise correct on rules 1 and 3. Filing a repair task assigned to tako (general work agent, presumed author) rather than fixing directly, per review-task authority.

children.title: Fix slugify.js: collapse dash runs and strip trailing dash
children.purpose: slugify/slugify.js fails SPEC.md rules 4 and 5. Rule 4 says runs of "-" must collapse to a single "-", but the implementation never collapses dashes at all: slugify("hello   world") returns "hello---world" instead of "hello-world", and slugify("a--b") (literal double dash in input) stays "a--b" instead of "a-b". Rule 5 says no leading or trailing "-", but only the leading-dash strip is implemented (slugify.js line 20, `while (out.charAt(0) === "-") out = out.slice(1);`); there is no matching trailing-dash strip, so slugify("hello ") returns "hello-" instead of "hello", and slugify("trailing-") stays "trailing-" instead of "trailing". Additionally note (lower confidence, worth checking while in the file): only " ", "\t", "\n" are treated as whitespace-to-hyphen (slugify.js line 13); other whitespace such as \r, \v, \f or Unicode whitespace is silently dropped rather than turned into "-", which may or may not satisfy the spec's "any whitespace" wording depending on intended scope — decide and document the intended whitespace set while fixing rules 4 and 5.
children.completion_criteria: slugify("hello   world") === "hello-world"; slugify("a--b") === "a-b"; slugify("hello ") === "hello"; slugify("trailing-") === "trailing"; slugify(" lead ") === "lead" (both ends). Existing tests in slugify/slugify.test.js still pass, and new test cases covering dash-collapsing and trailing-dash stripping are added to slugify.test.js. Whitespace-character handling (rule 2) is confirmed or fixed to match SPEC.md intent and documented in the code's spec comment if scope changed.
